question: In which of the following years, the Lucknow Session was organized in which the Muslim League signed an agreement with the Indian National Congress? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019))
options: 1885
1916
1900
1907
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1916

Explanation:
The Lucknow Session was organized in the year 1916. It is famous for the historic Lucknow Pact between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League. In this pact, both parties jointly demanded self-government from the British government. The Congress session was presided over by Ambika Charan Mazumdar. Under the Lucknow Pact, the Muslim League supported Congress's demands, while Congress accepted the Muslim League's demand for separate electorates. This pact became a symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity in Indian politics.

question: In the Battle of Plassey of 1757, who among the following has betrayed the Nawab of Bengal?  (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019))
options: Mir Jafar
Aurangzeb
Alivardi Khan
Sirajuddaula
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mir Jafar

Explanation:
The Battle of Plassey in 1757 was fought between the Nawab of Bengal Sirajuddaula and the British East India Company. The Nawab's commander-in-chief Mir Jafar betrayed him by conspiring with the British. He did not order his troops to fight, leading to Sirajuddaula's defeat. After the battle, Mir Jafar was installed as the Nawab of Bengal, and the Company gained significant political power in Bengal. This battle is considered the foundation of British colonial rule in India.

question: When the Indian National Congress (INC) had officially demanded an assembly to build the Constitution of India? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019))
options: 1920
1940
1945
1935
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1935

Explanation:
The Indian National Congress officially demanded an assembly to frame the Constitution of India for the first time in 1935. This demand was made in opposition to the Government of India Act 1935, as the Congress believed that Indians should have the right to draft their own constitution. Later, the demand was reiterated during the Cripps Mission in 1942. Ultimately, the Constituent Assembly was formed in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan, which adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949. The 1935 demand marks a significant milestone in the Indian freedom movement and constitutional development.

question: Which freedom fighter was known as 'Lokmanya'? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019) Shift 2)

question: Who among these was the first European to reach India by sea? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 3)

Before da Gama's discovery, routes to India were primarily overland or through Arab merchants. His journey laid the foundation for the Portuguese colonial expansion in Asia.

question: When was the partition of Bengal? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: 1904
1905
1906
1903
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1905

Explanation:
The partition of Bengal was carried out in 1905 by Lord Curzon. Its stated aim was administrative efficiency, but it effectively divided the Bengal Presidency into two parts – Eastern Bengal and Assam (Muslim-majority) and Western Bengal (Hindu-majority). This was seen as a part of the British divide and rule policy. The partition sparked widespread opposition, leading to the Swadeshi Movement and the Anti-Partition Movement. The partition was eventually annulled in 1911.

question: Who was the first Viceroy of India? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Lord Wellesley
Lord Canning
Lord Cornwallis
Lord Mayo
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lord Canning

Explanation:
The position of Viceroy in India was created directly under the British Crown after the Revolt of 1857. The Government of India Act 1858 ended the rule of the East India Company and transferred control to the British Crown. Lord Canning (1858-1862) became the first Viceroy of India. He was the Governor-General at the time of the transfer and was appointed as Viceroy. During his tenure, the Indian army was reorganized and financial reforms were introduced. Lord Wellesley, Lord Cornwallis, and Lord Mayo were Governors-General, but not Viceroys.

question: Who is called the first war of independence of India? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Sepoy Rebellion

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sepoy Rebellion

Explanation:
The first war of independence of India is the Sepoy Rebellion of 1857. It began on 10 May 1857 in Meerut and spread across northern India.
